newsitem.title: USA: BEFORE THE BELL - Signet Banking bid up.
newsitem.headline: BEFORE THE BELL - Signet Banking bid up.

text.p: Signet Banking Corp was bid higher in before markets opened Monday, boosted by its agreement to merge with First Union Corp in a $3.25 billion deal, traders said.
Signet was bid at 43 ahead of the opening, with an offer as high as 50, one said. Signet closed Friday at 36-11/16.

Volume was small, and First Union closed Friday at 97-7/16. The banks said Monday First Union had agreed to exchange 0.55 share for each Signet share, valuing Signet at about $53.59 a share, the banks said.

Among other active stocks, aircraft maker Boeing Co was trading at 54-1/2, down from a Friday close of 56. The company reported second-quarter earnings Monday of $0.48 a share against $0.68 the year before.
AT&T Corp was bid at 33 from a Friday close of 34-7/16. The long-distance company reported second-quarter earnings well below a year ago, but in line with Wall Street's reduced expectations.
Semiconductor maker Zilog Inc was bid at 23-3/4 from a Friday close of 22-8/16. The company has agreed to be acquired by Texas Pacific Group, a private investment partnership, for $25 a share.
